description:
Problem: oracle-gate.yml subscribes to issue_comment [created], and the gate job runs only when the comment body starts with 'Stand-in oracle review: APPROVE'. If an accepted stand-in is edited or deleted, the oracle-gate success it produced stays on the head until the hourly sweep or another event, so the pull request can merge on withdrawn evidence.

Outcome: the gate re-evaluates on an edited comment whose new body or previous body (github.event.changes.body.from) starts with the marker, and on a deleted comment whose body starts with the marker. Other comment edits and deletions neither run the gate nor join or cancel the pull request's gate concurrency group.

Decision gates (stop and report if one fails):
1. Read how decide() in _project/scripts/oracle_review_check.py treats stand-ins: exact text, attester list, and the unedited requirement. A fresh evaluation after an edit or deletion must reject the stand-in. If an edited stand-in is still accepted, stop: fixing that is a decision-rule change outside this item.
2. Confirm in GitHub's issue_comment payload docs that edited events carry changes.body.from and deleted events carry the deleted comment body. If not, stop and re-plan.

Item guardrails: keep the develop-only checkout and the dispatch-ref refusal. Extend the existing ignored-<run_id> concurrency keying so non-marker edits and deletions cannot cancel a running gate. Do not change the App binding, the decision rule, or the bridge job.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Close out with make pr-preflight, make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, then make pr-arm. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). Every behavior change gets a test that fails on the previous code.
